summary: In this excerpt from a fiction book (Book 14, part 37), the narrator Zen describes being questioned by two police officers and a conversation with Monica afterward. He explains that he first looked up Godwin after the FBI sent Wikipedia a takedown notice over an official seal image, and he admires Godwin's humorous letter. Over breakfast the group feels a brief sense of solidarity after standing up to police, though anxiety remains about Wilson and the authorities. Monica plans to teach a weekend class and meet Novak, while Zen worries about a possible warrant and plans to go out to meet the Group without telling her.
one_line: Zen recalls Godwin's humorous letter against the FBI, then discusses warrants and secret plans with Monica after police questioning.
key_facts: Zen says he first looked up Godwin when the FBI sent Wikipedia a takedown notice over a picture of their official seal.
Zen says the Encyclopaedia Britannica had the same seal picture in its article and was not made to take it down.
Zen says Godwin's letter argued the FBI was legally off base and was smart but funny.
Zen says he read Godwin's letter when he was about ten years old.
Zen says the best way to deal with an abuse of power is to make fun of it publicly, as Godwin figured.
Monica says Zen is strange, in a good way, after he mentions the letter.
Zen's dad said people whose houses are flooded or blown down in a tornado suddenly love their neighbors, though it usually does not last long.
Zen worries the police will return with a warrant and fears the authorities will screw everyone over.
Monica doubts a judge will sign off on a warrant on a Saturday.
Zen says the police are calling it a terrorist investigation and will pull out all the stops.
Monica calls the investigation security theatre, comparing it to making people take off their shoes at airports.
Monica has a weekend college class to teach and plans to meet Novak, who wants to go to a play that night.
Zen plans to go out that day to a meet-up with the Group and does not intend to tell Monica.
